text:
Anthony Mantha's season in New Jersey was going well until a throat fracture stopped it. NHL.com reported he's out at least a month, along with Johnathan Kovacevic, after surgery, and his last game was Nov. 7. The injury drew anger online; Sportskeeda's headline led with fans saying "Adam Pelech should be held accountable".

Before it, he was what the Devils hoped for. He had 5 goals and 10 points in 17 games on 13:28 a night, with a top shot speed in the 98th percentile. He'd come over after scoring 33 goals for Pittsburgh last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.5 wins above replacement, with expected wins even higher (2.6).

Our numbers saw more coming. New Jersey had scored 6.6 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, though his own shooting (23.8%) was well above his range. The Devils won eight of his last ten games. Now they need someone else's heavy shot in the middle six, and Mantha needs a clean recovery.
headline: Mantha's hot start, then surgery
